ai.description: Beddome’s Cat Snake reaches 1 meter. It is reddish-brown with dark, narrow crossbands and a distinct, dark Y-shaped mark on the head. It features a slender body and large, vertically elliptical pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Boiga beddomei* is best distinguished by its distinct, dark-edged vertebral spots and a characteristic Y-shaped mark on the nape, which lacks the continuous stripes of similar *Boiga* species.
ai.habitat: Beddome’s Cat Snake inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests across the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations ranging from 500 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Beddome's Cat Snake is primarily nocturnal and arboreal, using its slender body to navigate tree branches while actively hunting for small lizards and geckos at night.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Boiga beddomei* is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–9 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with eggs often deposited in tree hollows or leaf litter.
ai.distributionRemarks: Boiga beddomei is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, typically found in moist forests at elevations ranging from near sea level to approximately 1,500 meters.
